page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288 is an enterprise-grade virtual machine built for memory-intensive enterprise workloads and massive parallel processing. The server is powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem features a 504 MB L3 cache alongside advanced hardware vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX.

System memory totals 2232 GB of RAM, maintaining a high density ratio of 7.75 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations reflect this architectural scale, with uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 1063 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth measuring 412 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is top-tier, demonstrated by high-volume throughput in stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang compilation runs. The machine does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and contains no discrete GPU hardware.

Without accelerator silicon, generative LLM text generation throughput drops significantly despite support for CPU-driven AMX extensions. However, memory and database operations exhibit exceptional scale, delivering over 405 million Redis SET operations per second and strong static web serving throughput. Qualitative cost efficiency reflects high hardware consolidation value, allowing organizations to run large-scale in-memory databases, dense virtualization pools, and batch ETL jobs on a single unified compute node rather than distributed clusters.

Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288 is appropriate for memory-resident enterprise databases like SAP HANA and Redis, large-scale software compilation, big data analytics pipelines, and multi-threaded scientific simulations requiring extensive memory capacity without discrete GPU accelerators.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288 is a memory-dense compute instance engineered for high-capacity enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor on x86_64 architecture, it delivers 288 dedicated vCPUs across 144 physical cores running at 2.3 GHz, supported by 504 MB of L3 cache and AMX matrix instructions. The instance incorporates 2232 GB of system RAM, providing 7.75 GB per vCPU, while offering no bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute, Clang software builds, and uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 1063 GB/sec. Redis performance exceeds 405 million operations per second, confirming strong memory subsystem efficiency. Lacking local disks and hardware accelerators, it trades storage locality and LLM text generation efficiency for massive centralized memory density. This configuration is best suited for large in-memory databases, data analytics, batch ETL workloads, and high-core software build clusters.
